text:
Hana Park: quick update — did a cross-region kernel bridge test for onboarding the 13B family (quant q8/q5) to evaluate flashv2 -> flashv3 migration vs Triton vendor libs. wanted to surface hotspots and a recommended switchover heuristic.

Omar Diaz: nice, numbers? p50/p95/p99 and throughput for typical PLG payloads?

Hana Park: pasted the short summary below (batch=4, seq=512, prefix caching disabled to stress runtime). these are median of 3 runs each.

```
config: q8, batch=4, seq=512
us-east-1 (h100, flashv3): p50 27ms, p95 52ms, p99 130ms, tps 94
eu-west-1 (h100, flashv3): p50 33ms, p95 61ms, p99 185ms, tps 82
apac-northeast-1 (a100, triton-vendor): p50 46ms, p95 92ms, p99 260ms, tps 48

config: q5, batch=4, seq=512
us-east-1 (h100, flashv3-q5): p50 24ms, p95 48ms, p99 120ms, tps 102
eu-west-1 (h100, flashv3-q5): p50 30ms, p95 58ms, p99 160ms, tps 88
apac-northeast-1 (a100, triton-q5): p50 42ms, p95 88ms, p99 230ms, tps 54
```

Kai Nguyen: interesting that flashv3-q5 on h100 outperforms triton on a100 even in apac. was packing/conv config identical?

Hana Park: yes, identical user workload. kernel weight compiled with same aten ops, only difference is kernel impl. for apac we saw triton + a100 jitter on p99 during microbursts (traffic shape: lots of small single-turn chats).

Tanya Li: did you measure warmup behaviour? i'm worried about cold tails when autoscaling.

Hana Park: good call — warmup sketch: flashv3 reaches steady-state 2x faster than triton on h100. sample traces: first 10 requests have p95 ~200-300ms on triton/a100, but drop to stable after ~40 requests. flashv3 warms in ~10-12 reqs.

Leon Ortiz: any surprising memory/kv-cache interactions? Q5 sometimes blows up mem usage.

Hana Park: q5 reduces memory, but flashv3's kernel backend allocates slightly larger transient buffers for attention vs triton; on h100 that's fine, on a100 we saw occasional OOM-like soft failures when sequence length spikes to 1024. added small guard in runtime to force fallback to 4-bit packed path for >768 seq on a100.

Omar Diaz: what's your recommended switch heuristic then?

Hana Park: proposal: for h100 regions -> prefer flashv3 by default for q5/q8 unless explicit vendor-only requirement. criteria: 1) p95_latency_gain >= 10% AND 2) p99_latency_gain >= 15% OR throughput_gain >= 15% over vendor. for a100/APAC, keep triton-vendor as default for now but enable flashv3 as canary route for stable workloads (low seq variance).

Kai Nguyen: suggest adding occupancy and microburst tests to the gating. maybe require p99 under 2.5x baseline during 30s traffic spike to approve switchover.

Hana Park: +1. adding hysteresis: require 2 consecutive canary deployments (12h apart) with no regression and with traffic spikes simulated. also will add a perf flag `kernel_autoswitch: false` per deployment in console until we've validated.

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: model=llama2-chat-13b-quant-q5, region=us-east-1, pct=5 at 03:00 UTC (job 84022).

Tanya Li: please capture evaluation prompt-set (10k prompts) and save replay traces — we need those to run quality reg checks after switching.

Hana Park: saving prompt set to s3://redwood-bootcamp/benchmarks/llama2-13b/bridge-q5/ and linking to the PR. will also record perf traces and heatmaps.

Omar Diaz: TL;DR: move h100 regions to flashv3 for q5 if p99 and throughput criteria met, keep a100/apac on triton for now, enable canaries + hysteresis + simulated microburst gating.

Kai Nguyen: will add the microburst simulator to the repo and wire the CI perf job.

Hana Park: thanks all — i'll open a short playbook PR with the switch heuristics and a checklist for private customers (KMS, vendor policy notes).

Omar Diaz: :thumbsup:

Tanya Li: thx!
